To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
vetiver grass is a Cd excluders and bana grass is a Cd accumulator, and that vetiver grass can be considered as a potential candidate for phytoremeditation.

Cd contamination had no significant effect on growth, photosynthetic characteristics, and mineral nutrition in vetiver grass while Cd contamination had significant effect on the growth, mineral nutrition, Cd accumulation and translocation of bana grass.
the energy allocation characteristics and mineral nutrition characteristics of vetiver grass and bana grass may be useful in selecting suitable plant species for phytoextraction.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effects of cadmium (Cd) pollution on the growth, mineral nutrition, and photosynthetic characteristics of two grasses, namely, vetiver grass (VG, Vetiveria zizanoides) and bana grass (BG, Pennisetum americanum × P. purpureum).
the effect of Cd on the growth, mineral nutrition and photosynthesis of vetiver grass and bana grass and provides some useful information for phytoremedial application.

the differential effects of soil Cd pollution on the growth, mineral nutrition, metal accumulation and energy allocation in two different grass species, which may provide a basis for selecting suitable plants for phytoremeditation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Cd pollution decreased the biomass production and mineral nutrition, while it had no influence on photosynthetic rates of both the grass species.
vetiver grass is a suitable plant for phytostabilisation and bana grass is suitable for phytoreclamation.
vetiver grass is a suitable species for use in phytoremediating Cd-contaminated soils, and that bana grass is not suitable for use in this context.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Cd pollution significantly decreased Fe and Mn in the roots and translocation factors of K and Zn in the roots of the accumulator (bana grass), while it significantly decreased Fe in the roots of vetiver grass.
vetiver grass was an ideal Cd phytoremediator, while bana grass was a potential Cd accumulator. © CSIRO 2010.
vetiver grass is a suitable plant species for soil remediation by phytostabilization and/or rhizofiltration while bana grass is a suitable species for phytostabilisation and/or rhizodegradation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
vetiver grass is more suitable than bana grass for phytoremeditation of Cd-polluted soils.
the accumulation of Cd in plants can be reduced by selecting species that are not Cd accumulators.
vetiver grass is a suitable candidate for phytoremedation of soils contaminated by Cd.
